source.title: AL2: Progressive Activation Loss for Learning General Representations in Classification Neural Networks
source.authors: Majed El Helou; F. Dümbgen; S. Süsstrunk

record.file_problem: Complete paper text supplied; supplementary material is referenced but not included.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how an activation regularizer affects test accuracy on partially corrupted labels and a cumulative-ablation measure; it does not reproduce any listed version's specific method or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for an AL2 regularizer on data with 75% corrupted labels. The text says supplementary results cover other corruption rates and datasets, but does not provide them here. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Table 1 tests V6 in a new setting: a VGG-like CNN trained on MNIST with 75% corrupted labels. Comparing dropout alone with the bare network shows higher held-out accuracy at every reported epoch. The extracted rows instead compare adding AL2 within each regularizer condition and miss this dropout intervention. The AL2 and activation-ablation results do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they claim AL2 improves generalization assessments on three benchmark datasets and changes learned representations. The supplied numerical accuracy and ablation tables substantiate only MNIST with 75% corrupted labels; the additional classification results are deferred to supplementary material.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces progressive activation regularization and evaluates it on partially corrupted-label data; the text does not establish a match to an original version's recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported AL2 effect varies by baseline regularizer and training epoch; for example, dropout without AL2 has higher test accuracy at epochs 100–300, while AL2 has higher accuracy at later epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding AL2 improves epoch-700 test accuracy from 25.84% to 68.46% for the bare network, 25.55% to 81.16% with BN, 55.39% to 91.70% with dropout, and 25.57% to 86.98% with weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressive activation regularization improves final held-out accuracy in this partially corrupted-label setting; its effects depend on regularizer and training epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: AL2 increases epoch-700 cumulative activation-ablation area for all four regularizer configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AL2 improves the reported activation-ablation area on MNIST with 75% corrupted labels.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: Only the MNIST 75%-corruption results are included in the supplied text; other corruption rates and datasets are in supplementary material not supplied. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The cumulative-ablation score is a proxy assessment, not test error itself.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 training cross-entropy and activation-regularization-loss values are omitted, as are Table 2 results for epochs 100–600, to prioritize the reported test-accuracy outcomes and epoch-700 cumulative-ablation comparison within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No supplied natural-label versus fully randomized-label comparison establishing both memorization capacity and natural-label generalization under the same recipe. The reported corruption rate is 75%, not fully random labels.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget.

No training-set-size sweep, dropout-rate sweep establishing excessive-dropout underfitting, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Clean-label results are referenced in unavailable supplementary material.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure, ranking against norm or margin measures, or corresponding gap analysis.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: Add V6 rows comparing dropout alone against the bare network without AL2. At epochs 100–700, bare/dropout test accuracies (%) are 84.20/96.13, 45.30/96.47, 25.25/95.93, 23.83/92.74, 26.07/81.96, 26.45/68.12, and 25.84/55.39. These matched-dataset, matched-initialization comparisons are observed dropout benefits.
missing.locator: Section 4 and Table 1, Bare and DO test-accuracy entries before each slash.

missing.what: Add V6 comparisons holding AL2 fixed and introducing dropout. At epochs 100–700, bare+AL2/dropout+AL2 accuracies (%) are 95.25/94.43, 94.92/95.03, 93.07/95.03, 88.76/94.79, 79.64/92.15, 75.88/92.69, and 68.46/91.70. This shows the dropout effect also depends on checkpoint and concurrent regularization.
missing.locator: Table 1, Bare and DO test-accuracy entries after each slash.

record.verdict_notes: The reader incorrectly treats dropout solely as an irrelevant baseline: its direct comparison with the bare network tests V6. Existing AL2 contrasts should remain outside the listed versions. Their cannot_determine states concern claim applicability, not unreadable numbers. The additional AL2-fixed dropout comparison also warrants separate V6 verdict groups once its missing rows are added: epoch 100 is reversed, epoch 200 is a small positive change, and epochs 300–700 show increasing benefits. No uncertainty estimates establish the significance of the small early differences.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the version's natural-label versus fully randomized-label comparison or whether the same networks fit fully random labels and generalize on natural labels.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.
No dropout intervention testing the version's stated conditions; dropout appears only as a baseline, with or without AL2.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.

relationships.condition: VGG-like CNN on MNIST with 75% symmetric incorrect-label corruption; dropout alone versus no regularization, without AL2, at matched epochs.
relationships.reason: Based on Table 1 text and the missing dropout-comparison rows: dropout raises test accuracy at all seven checkpoints, including 84.20% to 96.13% at epoch 100 and 25.84% to 55.39% at epoch 700. Existing r1–r7 and r15–r21 contain the endpoints but encode AL2 interventions.
relationships.display_finding: Dropout reportedly raised test accuracy at every listed checkpoint, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
